messages:
sasha: Heads-up — we're seeing a flakey window where GH Actions runs terraform apply via Atlantis, but ArgoCD sync lags and pods start with old secrets. Anyone seen this pattern? wondering whether to add a post-apply step in the GH workflow to `argocd app wait && argocd app sync` or handle it elsewhere.
priya: yep saw this last week on staging. short answer: do a post-apply sync from GH Actions (not from Atlantis). Atlantis should be limited to TF state changes. mixing ArgoCD sync inside Atlantis causes lifecycle surprises. :+1:
tom: adding a tiny detail — secrets are managed with sops + KMS, and the controller (sops-secrets-controller) reconciles asynchronously. sometimes tf apply updates a k8s secret (or CR) and the controller takes a second to render. so if you sync immediately you may still get the old value. recommend: 1) wait-for argocd until resource conditions are healthy, 2) optionally add a short retry/backoff for resources that depend on secrets.
mae: concrete GH Actions step I used:

```
- name: Argocd post-apply sync
  run: |
    argocd login $ARGOCD_HOST --username $ARGOCD_USER --password $ARGOCD_PASS --insecure
    argocd app wait my-app --timeout 120s || true
    argocd app sync my-app --prune
    argocd app wait my-app --health --timeout 180s
```

works well when placed after the Atlantis apply approval job. note the `|| true` so the job doesn't hard-fail if wait times out — we still try sync.
sasha: good examples, thanks. question: is there any risk of race if GH Actions triggers a sync and ArgoCD's auto-sync is also enabled? could double-sync cause issues?
priya: not really — argocd will dedupe apply operations. the bigger risk is conflicting actors: if someone else is mid-rollout. add a lightweight lock (we use a tiny Dynamo table lock keyed by app name) or rely on GitOps flow where GH Actions pushes a manifest update commit and ArgoCD sees it. for TF-managed infra changes it's OK to do an imperative sync post-apply.
tom: important note about Atlantis: it runs under a service account that doesn't have access to cluster secrets controllers (we intentionally limit perms). so Atlantis can't wait on k8s controllers. GH Actions runner has the cluster creds and argocd creds so it's the right place for orchestration.
mae: also think about Secrets wiring: if you put secret rotation or templating in CI, ensure the sequence: terraform (update infra) -> secret controller reconcile -> ArgoCD sync -> app health check. if you need strict ordering, add small sleeps + retries or increase controller reconcile frequency.
deploy-bot: CI: workflow "infra/terraform-apply.yml" completed for repo infra-config (run #482). triggered post-apply job 'argocd-post-sync' at 1775123560.
sasha: sweet. plan: add the argocd post-apply step to the GH Actions workflow, include a handshake lock (simple S3/Dynamo lock) and bump timeouts. i'll draft a PR and ping for reviews. thanks all :rocket:
priya: leave a note in the PR describing the attack surface (why not Atlantis) and add a unit test for the GH Actions job env vars so we don't regress credentials.
tom: lgtm — if you want i can share our lock helper script. it's 20 lines.
mae: rmw: also consider switching to ExternalSecrets for runtime secrets so controllers reconcile faster — reduces TTLs. :sparkles:
